title: Sultanate of Muscat and Oman
capsule: Muscat and Oman was the ruling designation for the Al Bu Sa'id sultanate governing the southeastern Arabian Peninsula and a network of overseas possessions stretching to Zanzibar and coastal East Africa, following the formal split of the Al Bu Sa'id domain in 1861. Under Sultan Faisal bin Turki (r. 1888–1913) and his son Taimur bin Faisal (r. 1913–1932), the sultanate operated under increasing British paramountcy codified in successive treaties, while the interior remained contested between the coastal sultanate and the Ibadi imamate. The country was renamed the Sultanate of Oman in 1970 when Said bin Taimur was deposed by his son Qaboos, who launched systematic modernization.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Coastal territories are well documented through British Indian Office records; interior boundaries between the sultanate and the Ibadi imamate are imprecisely attested for much of this period.
